title: Port flushing and care
what: A nurse puts a special needle into the port and flushes it so no clots form inside.
why: Between chemotherapy courses when the port is not in use. Usually once every few weeks. The clinic will give you the schedule.
tell_doctor: If the port area hurts, is red or swollen
Whether you have had a fever
Allergy to antiseptic or adhesive tape

prepare.title: Schedule
prepare.text: Write down the date of the next flush. It must not be skipped.

prepare.title: Pain relief
prepare.text: If the needle is uncomfortable, ask about numbing cream. It is put on beforehand.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Clothes that give easy access to your chest.

bring: The date of your last flush
steps: The nurse examines the area and cleans the skin over the port
Feels for the port and inserts the special needle
Checks that blood flows back and the port works
The needle is removed and the spot is covered with a plaster
feel: A short prick through the skin
A cool feeling from the fluid, sometimes a taste in the mouth
after: You can take off the plaster after a few hours
Usually you can go straight back to your normal activities
Write down the date of the next flush
red_flags: Redness, pus or pain at the port site
Fever or chills after the flush
Swelling of the arm, neck or face

faq.q: How often does the port need to be flushed?
faq.a: Usually once every few weeks when the port is not in use. The clinic will give the exact schedule.

faq.q: What happens if I skip a flush?
faq.a: The port can get blocked by a clot. Then it is harder to use, and sometimes it has to be replaced.

reminders.text: Port flush tomorrow. Bring your port card and note the date of your last flush.
